Definition: from some (obsolete) base akin to that of αὐχέω (to boast) and G2172; to vaunt (in a good or a bad sense):--(make) boast, glory, joy, rejoice.
BiblicalUsage: Kauchaomai means to boast, to glory, to rejoice in something. Romans 5:11 says we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement. 1 Corinthians 1:29 says no flesh should glory in his presence, and 1 Corinthians 1:31 says, he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. Galatians 6:14 says, God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe boasting is only safe when the boast is the cross: everything else is flesh glorying in God's presence. I hold that joy in God is the right kind of glorying, because it gives him what he gave us. My position is Paul's: if I boast, let it be the cross.
